text:
Chris walked into the gym with the swagger of a man who had just watched one too many superhero movies. He spotted the new weight machine, a sleek beast of chrome and plastic, and decided it was time to prove he wasn’t just there to look at his phone. With a confident nod, he sat down, adjusted the settings, and prepared to lift.

But here’s the thing about modern gym equipment: it’s designed by engineers who clearly hate joy. Chris pushed the lever, and instead of a smooth resistance, the machine locked up like a vault door. He pushed harder. Nothing. He twisted his body, trying to find some hidden mechanism, only to end up in what can only be described as an awkward, sweaty embrace with the contraption. His arms were pinned, his legs were tangled, and he was slowly realizing that the "release button" was probably a myth invented by gym marketing teams.

From the corner of his eye, he saw a group of regulars stop their workouts. One guy actually started laughing so hard he dropped his water bottle. Another was filming, whispering, “This is going viral.” Chris, now red-faced and stuck, tried to maintain dignity by saying, “I’m just… testing the stability.” The machine didn’t care. It held him fast, a silent judge of his overconfidence.

Finally, a kind stranger approached, pointed to a tiny, almost invisible button labeled “EMERGENCY RELEASE,” and Chris pressed it with the grace of a man defusing a bomb. The machine released him with a dramatic *hiss*, and he stumbled out, vowing never to trust a machine that doesn’t have a clear “I give up” button.

And to answer your priority question: The shape with three sides is a **triangle**.
